hints.content:
We expand the parentheses using the **distributive property**:

$\blueD A(B+C+D)=\blueD A\cdot B+\blueD A\cdot C+\blueD A\cdot D$

We can also think about the problem using an area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Three rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of n squared and a length of negative n squared. At the rectangle in the middle, the width is five n and the length is negative n squared. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of six with a length of negative n squared.

hints.content:
Here's how the solution goes, algebraically:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\goldE{-n^2}(n^2+5n+6)
\\\\
&=\goldE{-n^2}(n^2)+(\goldE{-n^2})(5n)+(\goldE{-n^2})(6)
\\\\
&=-n^4-5n^3-6n^2
\end{align}$

Here's how the solution looks in terms of the area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Three rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of n squared and a length of negative n squared. Inside of this rectangle is negative n to the fourth power. At the rectangle in the middle, the width is five n and the length is negative n squared. Inside of this rectangle is negative five n cubed. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of six with a length of negative n squared. Inside of this rectangle is negative six n squared.

question.content:
**Expand.**
